newsitem.title: GERMANY: Head of Austrian imperial house injured in crash.
newsitem.headline: Head of Austrian imperial house injured in crash.

text.p: Otto von Habsburg, the eldest son of Austria's last emperor and head of the imperial house of Habsburg, was hurt in a car crash near the German town of Diessen on Sunday, police said. Local radio station BLR said his injuries were serious.
Habsburg, 84, has renounced his claim to the imperial throne, which Austria abolished after World War One in 1919, and has lived in southern Germany for the last 43 years.
He has published a number of historical works and has spent his latter years working for and writing about European integration.
He took German nationality alongside his Austrian citizenship has been a German member of the European parliament since 1979.
Tens of thousands of Viennese lined the streets of the capital in 1989 for the elaborate funeral procession of Otto von Habsburg's mother, the former empress Zita.
Last year Austria officially scrapped a law which had imposed nearly 80 years of exile on the members of the dynasty who had not formally renounced their claim to the throne.
Both Otto von Habsburg's two younger brothers, Felix and Carl-Ludwig, had until then held Austrian passports which included an addendum stating they could enter any country but their own.
